title: Bee motif
subtitle: A striped oval body with two oval wing panels and chain antennae, 8 cm
excerpt: The bee motif is a small striped oval body in yellow and black DK cotton with two translucent-style oval wing panels in white or cream and a pair of ch-6 antennae. At 8 cm long it is compact enough for greetings card embellishment and works at full scale as an applique on children's blankets and summer cushions.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from striped oval and wing construction. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 7 (1892), small animal applique chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A crochet bee applique in yellow and black DK cotton with two cream oval wings and chain antennae, 8 cm long, photographed flat on natural linen in soft daylight. Clearly recognisable bee silhouette.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished bee motif measures 8 cm long and 4 cm tall in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.caption: Oval body with yellow/black stripe rows. Two small oval wing panels in cream. Ch-6 antennae at the head end.

glossaryTerms.definition: Switching yarn colour at the start of a new row or round. In this bee, alternating yellow and black rows form the stripe body.

content.text: The bee body is a small oval worked from a chain foundation with three

— two rows yellow, one row black — to give the characteristic three black stripes. The wings are even smaller ovals in cream or white, worked in the same way as the body but without colour changes. The antennae are simple chain lengths with a small slip-stitch curl at the tip.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 5 g yellow DK cotton, 3 g black, 4 g cream for wings. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Black embroidery thread for the eye. Scissors.

content.text: Each finished bee motif measures 8 cm long and 4 cm tall in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.

In yellow, ch 10. Rnd 1: Dc in 2nd ch from hook, dc in next 6 ch, 3dc in last ch. Work along the underside: dc in next 6 ch, 2dc in the first ch. Sl st to first dc to join. (22 dc.) Rnd 2 (yellow): Ch 1. Dc around. Sl st to join. Change to black. Rnd 3 (black): Ch 1. Dc around. Sl st to join. Change to yellow. Rnd 4 (yellow): Ch 1. Dc around. Sl st to join. Fasten off.

In cream, ch 8. Dc in 2nd ch from hook, dc in next 4 ch, 3dc in last ch. Work along underside: dc in next 4 ch, 2dc in first ch. Sl st to join. (16 dc.) Work one more round of dc. Sl st to join. Fasten off with a 15 cm tail.
Attach black at the head end (narrow end) of the body. Ch 6. Sl st into the 2nd ch from hook. Fasten off. Rejoin for the second antenna and repeat.
Sew the two wing ovals to the upper body, one on each side, with the inner edge of each wing touching at the centre back. Embroider a small French knot eye near the antenna end.

definition.title: Bee motif
definition.caption: Oval body: ch-10, 22dc oval, stripes 2 yellow / 1 black. Wing: ch-8, 16dc smaller oval in cream. Antennae: ch-6 loops.

content.text: Weave in all ends. Sew the finished bee onto the base fabric through the body perimeter.
Handwash with the base fabric in cool water. Lay flat to dry.

The butterfly motif (crochet-animal-butterfly) uses a similar wing-and-body assembly at a larger scale. The sunflower motif (crochet-flower-sunflower) pairs naturally with bees for a summer meadow theme.
